Below is a conservative, OB-cleared, home-based 12‑week postpartum return program designed for a client who is 4 weeks post uncomplicated C‑section. It respects current restrictions (light activity only until 6 weeks; no direct “ab” work or heavy lifting). The plan emphasizes breathing, pelvic floor and deep core connection, posture, gentle mobility, walking, and progressive total-body strength using bodyweight. It includes phased progressions, clear guardrails, and options to regress or hold if symptoms arise.

Important safety notes
- Red flags: Stop and regress if there is increased vaginal bleeding, pelvic or abdominal pain/pressure/heaviness, bulging or doming along the midline, incision pain, increased lochia, dizziness, unusual fatigue, leaking that worsens, or low back pain that lingers. If symptoms persist, refer back to OB or pelvic health PT.
- Progress at the client’s symptom-guided pace. If any step aggravates symptoms, hold at the prior level for 3–7 days before retrying.
- Breathing/form are paramount. Every rep integrates 360° breathing with pelvic floor and deep core coordination.
- Incision care: avoid positions or pressures that strain the scar; support it with hands or a soft pillow when coughing/sneezing.

Structure overview
- Frequency: 4–6 days/week of very short sessions (10–30 minutes), combining walking + restorative mobility + core/pelvic floor work. Strength begins gently after 6 weeks and progresses gradually.
- Equipment: yoga mat; household support (chair/wall/counter). No external load through Week 6; then optional light household load (e.g., 1–3 kg) from Week 7+ if fully symptom-free.
- Breathing cueing for most exercises:
  - Inhale: 360° rib expansion, let pelvic floor and belly gently yield.
  - Exhale: gentle pelvic floor lift and lower belly “hug in” (imagine zipping up from sit bones to low belly), maintain neutral ribs/pelvis.

Phase summary
- Phase 1 (Weeks 4–6): Restore breathing, pelvic floor, posture; gentle mobility; walking tolerance. No direct abdominal strain or heavy lifting.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 7–9): Foundation strength (glutes, back, legs), progressive deep core endurance, anti-movement core, gait capacity.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 10–12): Build capacity and resilience; functional strength circuits; slightly higher RPE walking; introduce gentle tempo and holds.

Weekly details

Week 4 (current week)
Goals: Establish daily 360° breathing and pelvic floor awareness, reduce stiffness, begin short walks; zero abdominal strain.
- Walking: 10–15 minutes, 5–6 days/week, flat terrain, RPE 3–4/10. Break into 2 x 7–8 min if fatigued.
- Daily restorative (10–15 min, 5–6 days/week):
  1) 360° Crocodile breathing (prone, pillow under hips as needed): 6–8 breaths x 2–3 sets.
  2) Side-lying rib expansion breathing: 6–8 breaths/side x 2 sets.
  3) Pelvic floor awareness (hook-lying): on exhale, 20–30% gentle lift/zip; release fully on inhale. 5–6 breaths x 2–3 sets.
  4) Supine heel slides (tiny ROM, neutral spine, hand support on incision if needed): 6–8/side x 2 sets, exhale on slide.
  5) Seated scapular retraction + chin nods: 8–10 reps x 2 sets.
  6) Gentle mobility: cat-cow (small range), open books side-lying, calf/hip flexor light stretches 20–30 sec each.

Week 5
Goals: Maintain walk volume, add gentle glute/hip activation without abdominal bracing; refine breath/pelvic floor timing.
- Walking: 12–18 minutes, 5–6 days/week, RPE 3–4. Optional 1–2 short hills only if symptom-free.
- Restorative (12–18 min, 5–6 days/week):
  1) 90/90 supported breathing (feet on wall, hips/knees at 90): 6–8 breaths x 2–3 sets.
  2) Pelvic floor quick flicks: 5 gentle 1-sec lifts, 10–15-sec rest; 2–3 rounds. Then 3–4 slow 3–4-sec holds with full release.
  3) Supine marching (tiny ROM): 6–8/side x 2 sets, exhale to lift.
  4) Side-lying clamshells (no band): 8–10/side x 2–3 sets, exhale to open.
  5) Elevated counter push-ups (very high angle): 6–8 x 2 sets, exhale up; stop well before any doming.
  6) Child’s pose with wide knees + lateral reaches: 20–30 sec x 2.

Week 6
Goals: Prepare for clearance; slowly increase time-on-feet; add controlled bridges from floor if symptom-free.
- Walking: 15–20 minutes, 5–6 days/week, RPE 3–4.
- Restorative/Activation (15–20 min, 5–6 days/week):
  1) Seated bandless rows (towel around feet or isometric squeeze pulling elbows back): 8–10 x 2–3 sets.
  2) Glute bridge (short range): 8–10 x 2–3 sets; exhale to lift, avoid rib flare, no pain/pressure.
  3) Side-lying hip abduction: 8–10/side x 2 sets.
  4) Sit-to-stand from high chair: 6–8 x 2 sets, exhale to stand, use hands as needed.
  5) Bird dog arms only: 6–8/side x 2 sets, minimal trunk shift.
  6) Continue breathing drills and PF quick flicks/slow holds as in Week 5.

Check-in after 6-week OB visit: If cleared for progressive activity, proceed to Phase 2. If not, hold at Week 6 programming and re-check in 1–2 weeks.

Phase 2: Foundational capacity (Weeks 7–9)
Principles: Increase strength for daily tasks, introduce anti-movement core (no crunches), maintain breathing, avoid doming/pelvic pressure. Intensity RPE 5–6/10. 3–4 strength sessions/week (20–30 min), walking most days.

Week 7
- Walking: 20–25 minutes, 5–6 days/week, RPE 3–4; include 2 x 2-min brisk intervals if symptom-free.
- Strength A (2 days):
  1) Sit-to-stand (lower chair height as able): 3 x 8–10.
  2) Elevated incline push-up (table/counter): 3 x 6–10.
  3) Hip hinge to wall (hands on thighs, short range): 3 x 8–10, focus on glutes.
  4) Glute bridge (full, controlled): 3 x 8–12 + 2–3 sec pause at top.
  5) Bird dog (arm + opposite leg, small range): 2–3 x 5/side, exhale on reach.
- Strength B (1–2 days):
  1) Step-back supported lunge (hands on counter/chair): 3 x 6–8/side.
  2) Standing wall row (towel anchored on doorknob, gentle tension) or isometric row: 3 x 8–10.
  3) Side-lying clam to abduction combo: 2–3 x 8/side each.
  4) Dead bug arms-only to heel taps progression: 2–3 x 6–8/side, stop before doming.
  5) Farmer carry practice without load: posture walk 3 x 20–30 sec focusing on ribs over pelvis, gentle brace on exhale.

Week 8
- Walking: 22–28 minutes, 5–6 days/week; 3 x 2–3 min brisk intervals, RPE up to 5.
- Strength A:
  1) Squat to chair with tempo (3-sec down): 3 x 8–10.
  2) Incline push-up: 3 x 8–10; lower incline slightly if perfect form/symptom-free.
  3) Hip hinge reach (counterbalance with arms): 3 x 8–10.
  4) Bridge march (alternating heel lift at top, minimal pelvis shift): 3 x 6–8/side.
  5) Pallof press isometric at wall (bandless: press forearms into wall, step out slightly): 3 x 20–30 sec holds.
- Strength B:
  1) Reverse lunge to knee tap (supported): 3 x 6–8/side.
  2) Quadruped row isometric (press hand into floor, pull opposite elbow toward hip without moving): 3 x 8–10/side.
  3) Side plank from knees (very short lever) or modified side-lying lift: 3 x 10–20 sec/side, no doming.
  4) Dead bug heel taps: 3 x 6–8/side.

Week 9
- Walking: 25–30 minutes, 5–6 days/week; 4 x 2–3 min brisk intervals, RPE 5.
- Strength A:
  1) Split squat (supported as needed): 3 x 6–8/side.
  2) Incline push-up: 3 x 8–12.
  3) Hip hinge to “good morning” (hands at chest): 3 x 10–12.
  4) Bridge with mini band alternative: if no band, add 5-sec isometric squeeze at top, 3 x 8–10.
  5) Bird dog longer reach: 3 x 6–8/side.
- Strength B:
  1) Step-ups to sturdy step (8–12 inches; use railing/wall): 3 x 8/side.
  2) Wall “Pallof” press (progress step-out distance): 3 x 8–10 with 3-sec hold.
  3) Side plank from knees (increase to 20–30 sec) or suitcase carry drill without load: 3 x 20–30 sec/side.
  4) Dead bug alternating arms/legs (short ROM): 3 x 6–8/side.

Phase 3: Capacity and function (Weeks 10–12)
Principles: Consolidate strength, improve endurance and posture under gentle load. Introduce optional light household load (1–3 kg, e.g., water bottle/backpack) if fully symptom-free. RPE 5–7. 3–4 strength sessions/week, walking with intervals.

Week 10
- Walking: 28–35 minutes, 5–6 days/week; 4–5 x 2–3 min brisk intervals, RPE 5–6.
- Total-body Circuit (2–3 days; 2–3 rounds, rest 60–90 sec between moves as needed):
  1) Goblet squat pattern holding 1–3 kg object at chest (or bodyweight): 8–10.
  2) Hip hinge with object (touch to thighs): 8–10.
  3) Step-up (hold rail/object at chest if using load): 8/side.
  4) Incline push-up: 8–12.
  5) Bridge march or single-leg bridge (short ROM): 6–8/side.
  6) Half-kneeling anti-rotation press at wall: 20–30 sec/side.
- Accessory (1 day):
  - Side plank from knees with top-leg straight (if tolerated): 2–3 x 15–25 sec/side.
  - Bird dog with 2–3 sec pause: 2–3 x 6/side.
  - Scapular Y/T/W prone or standing: 8–10 each.

Week 11
- Walking: 30–38 minutes; include 1 longer brisk block of 8–10 minutes, RPE up to 6 if symptom-free.
- Circuit A (2 days; 3 rounds):
  1) Split squat or supported reverse lunge (optional light load): 6–8/side.
  2) Hip hinge (optional load): 10–12.
  3) Incline push-up (lower angle): 8–12.
  4) Step-down eccentrics (slow 3-sec lower): 6–8/side.
  5) Pallof press hold or suitcase carry with 1–2 kg for posture: 20–30 sec/side.
- Circuit B (1–2 days; 2–3 rounds):
  1) Squat to small jump preparation (no leaving ground; calf raise at top): 8–10, prioritize control.
  2) Single-leg RDL reach (bodyweight, wall support): 6–8/side.
  3) Row isometric or backpack row (very light): 8–10.
  4) Side plank from knees 20–30 sec/side.
  5) Dead bug alternating with longer exhale: 6–8/side.

Week 12
- Walking: 30–40 minutes; option for 2 x 8–10 min brisk blocks, RPE 6–7 if completely symptom-free.
- Strength Circuit (3 rounds):
  1) Squat (goblet or BW) 10–12.
  2) Hip hinge (RDL pattern) 10–12.
  3) Step-up or split squat 8–10/side.
  4) Incline push-up 10–12.
  5) Bridge single-leg (controlled) 6–8/side.
  6) Anti-rotation press or suitcase carry 30–40 sec/side.
- Finisher (optional, if feeling great): 5-minute gentle EMOM
  - Minute 1: Marching in place with posture 45 sec.
  - Minute 2: Wall sit 30–45 sec.
  - Minute 3: Standing YTWs 10 reps each.
  - Minute 4: Calf raises 12–15.
  - Minute 5: Box breathing 4-4-4-4.

Daily/weekly recovery and mobility (all phases)
- Mobility (5–10 min most days): thoracic open books, cat-cow (small range early), hip flexor stretch, calf/hamstring stretches, doorway pec stretch 20–30 sec each.
- Scar and posture: once cleared by OB (usually after 6 weeks), gentle scar desensitization/massage as advised; frequent posture resets (ribs stacked over pelvis, soft knees).
- Sleep: prioritize naps and nighttime strategies; training volume is flexible around sleep quality.
- Hydration: aim for 2–3 liters/day; more if breastfeeding.
- Pelvic floor relaxation: equal emphasis on full release as on engagement; include 1–2 “downtraining” sessions/day (slow 6–8 breath cycles focusing on softening pelvic floor).

Breath/core integration coaching cues
- Exhale on exertion: standing up, pressing, stepping up, hinging up.
- Keep ribs stacked over pelvis; avoid breath-holding (no Valsalva).
- Watch midline: stop or regress if doming/bulging or pelvic heaviness appears.

Return-to-activity checkpoints
- End of Week 6: walking 20 minutes at RPE ≤4, basic bridges/clams without symptoms.
- End of Week 9: tolerate incline push-ups, step-ups, anti-rotation holds without doming/heaviness.
- End of Week 12: ready to discuss progressive jogging impact prep (if desired), higher-load strength, or class-based training, pending pelvic health PT/OB input.

Nutrition basics (general, adjust for breastfeeding and OB guidance)
- Emphasize protein at each meal (aim ~20–30 g), fiber-rich carbs, and healthy fats to support recovery.
- If breastfeeding: add ~300–500 kcal/day as needed for energy and milk supply; hydrate well; monitor any sensitivities in infant.
- Micronutrients: continue prenatal or postnatal multivitamin per OB; ensure iron, choline, DHA, and calcium adequacy.

Customization and regressions
- If any move triggers symptoms, reduce range, add more support (higher incline, hands on counter, shallower squat), slow tempo, or swap to an easier pattern (e.g., bridge instead of single-leg bridge).
- Spend extra time in Weeks 4–6 content if recovery feels behind; there is no rush.

This plan keeps her within “light activity only” until her 6-week check, then progresses gradually with clear symptom-based guardrails for a safe, confident return.

Here’s a simple, flexible postpartum nutrition plan to support milk supply, recovery, and energy for the 12-week program. It assumes no medical contraindications and that her OB is comfortable with breastfeeding-focused guidance. Encourage intuitive eating and symptom-guided adjustments.

Key principles
- Energy: Start with +300–500 kcal/day above her estimated maintenance while exclusively breastfeeding. Prioritize performance, satiety, and milk supply over weight loss in the first 12 weeks.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight per day (rough guide: 20–35 g per meal, 10–20 g per snack) to support tissue repair and satiety.
- Carbohydrates: 45–55% of calories from mostly fiber-rich, minimally processed sources to fuel milk production and training. Include carbs at every meal and around walks/workouts.
- Fats: 25–35% of calories, favoring mono- and polyunsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, seeds, avocado, fatty fish) to support hormones and milk fat quality.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L fluids/day. Use thirst + pale yellow urine as guides. Add ~250–500 mL during/after each feeding session and workouts. Herbal teas and milk count; limit caffeine to 200–300 mg/day if sensitive infant.
- Micronutrients: Continue prenatal/postnatal multivitamin per OB. Ensure adequate choline (~450–550 mg), DHA/EPA (at least 200–300 mg DHA/day), iodine (220–290 mcg), calcium (1,000 mg), iron (as advised by OB), vitamin D (check blood levels; often 1,000–2,000 IU/day or per provider).
- Gentle timeline: Prioritize supply and recovery for 6–8 weeks before any deliberate calorie cuts. If weight loss is a goal later, reduce by no more than ~250 kcal/day and monitor supply.

Daily structure (example plate method)
- Each main meal:
  - Protein: palm-size 1–2 servings (20–35 g).
  - Carbs: 1–2 cupped-hand servings (whole grains, potatoes, fruit, legumes).
  - Veggies/fruit: 2+ fistfuls (mix colors; include leafy greens).
  - Fats: 1–2 thumb-size servings (or 1/4–1/2 avocado, small handful nuts).
- Each snack: pair protein (10–20 g) with carbs/fiber or healthy fat.
- Around training: Small carb + protein snack 30–60 min before walks/strength; protein-rich meal within 1–2 hours after.

Sample day (adjust portions to hunger, size, and supply)
- On waking: 300–500 mL water; optional small snack if hungry (Greek yogurt + berries).
- Breakfast: Veggie omelet (2–3 eggs) + whole-grain toast with avocado; orange; water or milk.
- Snack: Oats with milk, chia/flax, banana, and peanut butter.
- Lunch: Chicken thigh or tofu bowl: quinoa or brown rice, roasted veggies, olive oil, and feta; side salad.
- Snack: Cottage cheese or hummus with whole-grain crackers and carrots; handful of walnuts.
- Dinner: Salmon (or sardines) with sweet potato and broccoli drizzled with tahini; mixed greens.
- Before bed (optional): Kefir or protein smoothie with fruit and oats if evening hunger is high.

Breastfeeding-specific supports
- Galactagogue foods: Oats, barley, fenugreek (if tolerated), fennel, ginger, brewer’s yeast, dark leafy greens, almonds. Evidence is mixed; use as enjoyable extras, not as sole strategy.
- Electrolytes: Consider adding a light electrolyte mix (low sugar) or a pinch of salt to water, especially on hot days or higher-walk days.
- Fish and mercury: 2 servings/week of low-mercury fatty fish (salmon, sardines, trout). Avoid high-mercury fish (shark, swordfish, king mackerel, tilefish).
- Caffeine/alcohol: Keep caffeine moderate (≤200–300 mg/day). If drinking alcohol, wait ~2–3 hours per standard drink before nursing or follow OB guidance.

Meal-prep shortcuts for new moms
- Batch proteins: Roast chicken thighs, tofu, or lentils; canned salmon/tuna (low mercury), rotisserie chicken.
- Freezer staples: Pre-cooked rice or quinoa, frozen veggies/berries, whole-grain waffles, turkey meatballs, bean soups.
- One-handed snacks: String cheese, trail mix, fruit, yogurt tubes, energy bites (oats, nut butter, seeds).
- Hydration cues: Keep a 1 L bottle at nursing station; drink when baby feeds.

Fiber and digestion
- Aim 25–35 g/day from fruits, veggies, legumes, whole grains; add gradually to avoid GI upset.
- Include probiotics/fermented foods (kefir, yogurt, kimchi) and prebiotics (bananas, onions, oats).
- If constipation: extra fluids, prunes/kiwi, chia seeds, warm beverages; consult OB if persistent.

Food safety and allergens
- Reheat leftovers to steaming hot; avoid unpasteurized cheeses and deli meats unless heated.
- If baby shows signs of sensitivity (rashes, GI distress), consider a short food/symptom diary and discuss with pediatrician before broad eliminations.

Simple tracking and adjustments
- Use a “3 S’s” weekly check:
  - Supply: baby satisfied, appropriate diaper counts and weight gain.
  - Strength: energy steady through workouts; no excessive soreness.
  - Satiety: hunger managed; not ravenous between meals.
- If supply dips: increase fluids, add 1–2 snacks/day (200–400 kcal), emphasize carbs, add an extra nursing/pumping session, rest more.
- If low energy: assess sleep, bump carbs around workouts, ensure iron and B12 are adequate.
- If weight loss is too fast (>0.5 kg/week) or energy tanks: increase calories by 200–300/day.

Grocery list starter
- Proteins: eggs, Greek yogurt/kefir, cottage cheese, chicken thighs, salmon/sardines, tofu/tempeh, lentils/beans, nut butters.
- Carbs: oats, brown rice/quinoa, whole-grain bread/tortillas, potatoes/sweet potatoes, fruit (berries, bananas, oranges), beans.
- Fats: olive oil, avocados, nuts/seeds (walnuts, chia, flax), tahini.
- Veggies: leafy greens, broccoli, peppers, carrots, onions, frozen mixed veg.
- Extras: iodized salt, prenatal/postnatal multivitamin, DHA supplement (if not eating fish), electrolyte mix, spices/herbs.

Integration with her 12-week program
- Weeks 4–6: Focus on consistency, hydration, easy-to-digest meals; aim upper end of calorie range if supply uncertain.
- Weeks 7–9: Maintain protein target; add a pre-session snack (e.g., banana + peanut butter or yogurt + granola).
- Weeks 10–12: Keep protein high; if she desires gradual fat loss and supply is robust, consider a very small calorie trim (≤250/day) and monitor for any supply changes.

Always defer to her OB/pediatrician for individualized needs, especially if there’s anemia, thyroid concerns, or infant sensitivities.

Great—here’s how to layer in progressive strength across the 12-week plan you’re already using, with clear week-by-week loads, tempos, and volume targets. It stays symptom-led and C‑section–aware, and uses only home resources (mat, chair, wall/counter, backpack/water bottles for load).

Global rules for progression
- RPE targets: Weeks 4–6 = 3–4; Weeks 7–9 = 5–6; Weeks 10–12 = 6–7.
- Add stress one variable at a time: form → range → tempo/pauses → reps → sets → load → stability (unilateral) → incline/lever changes.
- Progression trigger: When she can complete top reps with perfect breath/form and no symptoms two sessions in a row, progress 1 step (not all).
- Deload/hold: If symptoms (doming, heaviness, leaking, incision pulling) or lingering back/pelvic pain occur, reduce ROM, increase support, or step back 1–2 weeks.

Phase 1: Restore and prepare (Weeks 4–6)
- Frequency: 5–6 short movement days, 10–20 minutes. RPE 3–4.
- Strength emphasis: activation and positions (no external load).
- Main patterns and progress details:
  - Sit-to-stand from high chair: 2–3 x 6–8; slow 2–3 sec down; exhale to stand.
  - Elevated push-up at high counter: 2–3 x 6–8; rib stack, no breath-hold.
  - Short-range bridge: 2–3 x 8–10; 1–2 sec pause at top.
  - Hip hinge to wall touch (hands on thighs): 2 x 8–10.
  - Side-lying clam and abduction: 2–3 x 8–10/side.
  - Bird dog arms-only → add legs by end of Week 6 if zero symptoms: 2 x 6–8/side.
- Tempo focus: 3-1-2-0 on squats/hinge/bridge (down–pause–up–pause).
- Goal by end of Week 6: Comfortable with 3 x 10 bodyweight squats to chair, 3 x 10 bridges, 3 x 8 incline push-ups at high counter.

Phase 2: Foundational strength (Weeks 7–9)
- Frequency: 3–4 strength sessions/week, 20–30 minutes. RPE 5–6.
- Loading: Introduce light external load from household items (1–3 kg total) from Week 7 if fully symptom-free. Use a backpack with books/water bottles or a single water jug held goblet-style.
- Weekly progression map:
  Week 7 (form + range)
  - A Day
    1) Sit-to-stand (lower chair if good form): 3 x 8–10, tempo 3-1-2-0.
    2) Incline push-up (counter): 3 x 6–10.
    3) Hip hinge reach (counterbalance arms): 3 x 8–10.
    4) Bridge (full) with 2–3 sec pause: 3 x 8–12.
    5) Bird dog (short reach): 2–3 x 5–6/side.
  - B Day
    1) Supported reverse lunge (light fingertip support): 3 x 6–8/side.
    2) Towel/isometric row at wall or doorknob: 3 x 8–10 with 3-sec squeeze.
    3) Clam → abduction combo: 2–3 x 8/side each.
    4) Dead bug heel taps (short ROM): 3 x 6–8/side.
  - Optional light load: 1–2 kg goblet for sit-to-stand, only if zero symptoms and great control.
  Progression cue: If all sets land ≤RPE 5 with pristine form twice, add 2 reps per set next session.

  Week 8 (add tempo and light load)
  - A Day
    1) Squat to chair, 3-sec eccentric: 3 x 8–10; optional 1–3 kg goblet.
    2) Incline push-up (slightly lower surface if form holds): 3 x 8–10.
    3) Hip hinge (RDL pattern) with 1–3 kg object: 3 x 8–10; keep lats on, ribs stacked.
    4) Bridge march: 3 x 6–8/side.
    5) Pallof press isometric at wall: 3 x 20–30 sec.
  - B Day
    1) Supported reverse lunge: 3 x 8/side; add 1–2 kg goblet if ready.
    2) Isometric row progress (step back more): 3 x 10 with 3-sec squeezes.
    3) Side plank from knees: 3 x 10–20 sec/side.
    4) Dead bug heel taps: 3 x 8/side.
  Progression cue: Keep reps, add a second of pause at the hard point (bottom of squat, hinge mid-shin).

  Week 9 (add volume or small load bump)
  - A Day
    1) Split squat (supported): 3 x 6–8/side; optional 1–3 kg goblet.
    2) Incline push-up: 3 x 8–12 (lower angle if 12 easy).
    3) Hip hinge (RDL): 3 x 10–12 with 1–3 kg.
    4) Bridge with 5-sec squeeze at top: 3 x 8–10.
    5) Bird dog longer reach: 3 x 6–8/side.
  - B Day
    1) Step-ups to sturdy step (8–12 in): 3 x 8/side, load optional.
    2) Wall anti-rotation press (step-out farther): 3 x 8–10 with 3-sec hold.
    3) Side plank from knees 20–30 sec or suitcase carry drill (posture walk) 3 x 30 sec/side, no load or 1 kg.
    4) Dead bug alt arms/legs: 3 x 6–8/side.
  Progression cue: Choose one—add 1 kg load OR +2 reps per set on squats/hinges/lunges.

Phase 3: Capacity and resilience (Weeks 10–12)
- Frequency: 3–4 strength sessions/week; circuits for efficiency. RPE 6–7.
- Loading: 2–6 kg total household load as tolerated (goblet/backpack/jugs). Still prioritize breath/form and symptoms.
- Weekly progression map:
  Week 10 (introduce circuits and carries)
  - Total-body Circuit, 2–3 rounds, rest 60–90 sec between moves:
    1) Goblet squat 2–6 kg: 8–10.
    2) Hip hinge (RDL) 2–6 kg: 8–10.
    3) Step-up: 8/side, hold load at chest if stable.
    4) Incline push-up (lower angle): 8–12.
    5) Bridge march or short-ROM single-leg bridge: 6–8/side.
    6) Half-kneeling anti-rotation press at wall: 20–30 sec/side.
  - Accessory (optional 4th day):
    - Side plank from knees with top leg straight: 2–3 x 15–25 sec/side.
    - Bird dog with 2–3 sec pause: 2–3 x 6–8/side.
    - Scapular Y/T/W: 8–12 each.
  Progression cue: Add a round (from 2 to 3) before adding load.

  Week 11 (increase unilateral demand and eccentric control)
  - Circuit A, 3 rounds:
    1) Supported reverse lunge or split squat, 2–6 kg: 6–8/side, 3-sec lower.
    2) RDL 2–6 kg: 10–12.
    3) Incline push-up (as low as coffee table if zero symptoms): 8–12.
    4) Step-down eccentrics (slow 3-sec lower): 6–8/side.
    5) Suitcase carry 2–4 kg (one side), ribs stacked: 20–30 sec/side.
  - Circuit B, 2–3 rounds:
    1) Squat to calf raise (no jump): 8–10.
    2) Single-leg RDL reach (BW, wall support): 6–8/side.
    3) Backpack row (very light, or isometric): 8–12.
    4) Side plank from knees: 20–30 sec/side.
    5) Dead bug alternating with long exhale: 6–8/side.
  Progression cue: Add 1–2 kg to goblet/RDL if reps are strong and breathing steady.

  Week 12 (consolidate and set up next phase)
  - Strength Circuit, 3 rounds, RPE 6–7:
    1) Goblet squat 3–6 kg: 10–12.
    2) RDL 3–6 kg: 10–12.
    3) Split squat or step-up 2–4 kg: 8–10/side.
    4) Incline push-up (lowest safe angle): 10–12.
    5) Single-leg bridge (controlled): 6–8/side.
    6) Anti-rotation press or suitcase carry 3–5 kg: 30–40 sec/side.
  - Optional finisher (if totally symptom-free): 5-minute on-the-minute block
    - 45 sec marching in place (posture + gentle brace)
    - 30–45 sec wall sit
    - 10 standing YTWs
    - 12–15 calf raises
    - 60–90 sec relaxed box breathing

Breath and core coordination (apply to all sets)
- Inhale to prepare (ribs expand 360°, pelvic floor softens).
- Exhale on exertion (stand/press/pull), gentle pelvic floor lift and lower-belly wrap.
- Avoid breath-holding and rib flare; stop if midline doming or pelvic pressure appears.

Checkpoints for progression readiness
- Week 6 → 7: No pain/pressure with bridges, sit-to-stand, incline push-ups; walking 20 min RPE ≤4.
- Week 9 → 10: Step-ups, anti-rotation holds, and bird dogs symptom-free next day.
- Week 12 exit criteria: Circuits done at RPE ≤7, no symptoms during/after; ready for next block (heavier loads, lower inclines, impact prep with pelvic health PT/OB input).

Programming notes for you, the trainer
- Session structure (20–30 min): 5 min breath/mobility warm-up → 15–20 min main lifts (2–3 sets each or 2–3 circuit rounds) → 3–5 min cool-down and downtraining breaths.
- If time-crunched: Use EMOM/AMRAP-ish micro circuits but keep RPE ≤7 and breathing crisp.
- Regression toolbox: Raise incline, shorten ROM, add support (counter/chair), slow tempo, swap unilateral to bilateral, or reduce load.

This integrates progressive, C‑section–aware strength while honoring the original walking and core-coordination focus, ensuring a safe ramp back to fuller training after 12 weeks.

Short answer: start “core” right away—but it must be deep-core rehab, not traditional abs. Add direct abdominal training only after her 6-week check, when she’s symptom-free and can coordinate breath/pelvic floor without doming or pelvic pressure. Progress in layers.

How to phase core safely

Now through Week 6 (cleared for light activity only)
- Goal: reconnect diaphragm, pelvic floor, and deep abdominals (transversus abdominis) without increasing intra‑abdominal pressure.
- What to do:
  - 360° breathing with gentle pelvic floor lift on exhale, full release on inhale (daily).
  - Gentle TVA activations synced to breath: exhale to “zip up” low belly; inhale to release.
  - Core-adjacent patterns: heel slides, supine marching (tiny ROM), bridges (short range), bird‑dog arms only, side‑lying clams. All symptom-led.
- What to avoid: crunches, sit-ups, planks, leg lifts, bicycles, V‑sits, heavy bracing, or any move that causes midline doming/coning, incision pulling, pelvic heaviness, leaking, or increased bleeding.

After 6-week OB clearance (Weeks 7–9): introduce “anti-movement” core
Prereqs to start
- Can perform bridges, sit-to-stand, and incline push-ups with perfect breath and no symptoms.
- No visible doming along the midline with exhale/effort.

Week-by-week core plan
- Week 7
  - Dead bug progressions: arms-only → heel taps; 2–3 x 6–8/side.
  - Bird dog (short reach): 2–3 x 5–6/side, 2-sec pause.
  - Pallof press isometric at wall (bandless variant pressing forearms/hands into wall): 2–3 x 20–30 sec.
  - Side plank from knees (short lever): 2–3 x 10–15 sec/side.
- Week 8
  - Dead bug alternating arms/legs (short ROM): 3 x 6–8/side.
  - Bridge march: 3 x 6–8/side.
  - Pallof press holds: 3 x 20–30 sec (step a little farther from wall).
  - Side plank from knees: 3 x 15–25 sec/side.
- Week 9
  - Dead bug alternating with longer exhales: 3 x 8/side.
  - Bird dog longer reach: 3 x 6–8/side.
  - Suitcase carry drill (posture walk, no or very light load): 3 x 20–30 sec/side.
  - Side plank from knees: 3 x 20–30 sec/side.

Weeks 10–12: add challenge, still avoid high-pressure moves if any symptoms
- Week 10
  - Half-kneeling anti-rotation press (at wall or with very light band/object): 3 x 20–30 sec/side.
  - Side plank from knees with top leg straight: 2–3 x 15–25 sec/side.
  - Dead bug with 2–3 sec pauses: 3 x 6–8/side.
- Week 11
  - Suitcase carries (1–3 kg): 3 x 20–30 sec/side.
  - Modified front plank on elevated surface (hands on counter, body straight), 10–20 sec x 2–3, only if zero doming/pressure.
  - Single‑leg bridge (short ROM): 3 x 6–8/side.
- Week 12
  - Front plank progression: counter → sturdy table → high box, 15–25 sec x 2–3 holds; stop if doming.
  - Side plank from feet but knees slightly bent (if fully symptom-free): 2–3 x 10–20 sec/side.
  - Dead bug with heel extensions farther from body: 3 x 8/side.

When to reintroduce traditional “abs” (crunches/sit-ups/hollow work)
- Earliest: after 12 weeks postpartum and only if:
  - No diastasis doming at midline during curls.
  - No pelvic heaviness/pressure or leaking during/after core work.
  - She can hold a 20–25 sec front plank on a low incline with normal breathing and good rib–pelvis stack, and perform 8–10 slow dead bugs and 8–10 controlled bird dogs symptom-free.
- Start with: mini curl-ups (exhale to lift head/shoulders, hands supporting thighs), heel taps, low bicycle taps (tiny ROM), and very short planks (10–15 sec) on the floor. 2 sets of 6–8 each, 2–3 times/week. Build slowly.

Screening and guardrails
- Watch for: midline doming/coning, bulging at the scar, tugging/pain at incision, pelvic heaviness/pressure, increased lochia, back/hip pain. If present, stop, regress, and consider referral to a pelvic health PT.

Why wait

Readiness checklist for HIIT (all yes for 1–2 weeks in a row)
- No pelvic heaviness/pressure, leaking, or increased bleeding with brisk walking intervals up to RPE 7.
- No visible midline doming/coning during exertion; scar feels comfortable (no pulling/pain).
- Strength benchmarks:
  - 10–12 incline push-ups at a low angle with steady breathing.
  - 10 controlled split squats/side with light load.
  - 10 step-downs/side from 8–10 in step, no pain or collapse.
  - Holds: 20–25 sec front plank on a low incline and 30–40 sec side plank (knees or staggered).
- Walk tolerance: 35–40 minutes steady at RPE 4–5 and intervals such as 12 x 60 sec fast walk/60 sec easy without symptoms.
- Ideally, green light from OB and/or pelvic health PT.

How to add HIIT safely (Weeks 13–16 example)
- Frequency: 1 session/week for 2–3 weeks, then up to 2/week if fully symptom-free. Keep a recovery day or low-RPE walk the day after.
- Duration: 15–22 minutes total per session. Hard work time 6–10 minutes total.
- Intensity: Build from RPE 7–8 toward brief RPE 8–9 efforts. She should recover to conversational breathing between bouts.

- Week 13: 10 x 30 sec hard (fast uphill walk, high-incline treadmill, step-ups) / 60 sec easy. Warm up 5 min, cool down 5 min.
- Week 14: 12 x 30 sec hard / 45 sec easy OR 8 x 45 sec hard / 60 sec easy.
- Week 15: 10 x 45 sec hard / 60 sec easy OR 6 x 60 sec hard / 60 sec easy.
- Week 16: Pyramid 30–45–60–45–30 sec x 2 with equal rest. Optional small load for step-ups (1–3 kg) if zero symptoms.

Impact/plyometric HIIT (jog/low hops) prerequisites and intro
- Add only if she passes the readiness checklist AND:
  - Can perform: 20 calf raises/side, 20 seconds single-leg balance/side, 10 controlled single-leg RDL reaches/side, and tolerate quick walking downhills without symptoms.
- Intro session (choose one, 1/week at first):
  - Walk–jog HIIT: 10 x 30 sec jog (RPE 7–8) / 60–90 sec walk. Flat surface. Stop if heaviness or leaking.
  - Low-hop circuit: 20 sec gentle line hops side-to-side + 40 sec march, 6–8 rounds. Keep torso stacked, land softly, tiny hop height.
- Progress every 1–2 weeks by adding 1–2 rounds or extending hard intervals by 10–15 sec, not both.

Core and breath strategy during HIIT
- Exhale through the hardest part of each effort; think “exhale on impact.”
- Keep ribs stacked over pelvis; avoid breath holding.
- If any doming/pressure appears, downshift intensity immediately.

Red flags = pause HIIT and regress for 1–2 weeks
- Pelvic heaviness/pressure, leaking, increased bleeding, incision/scar pain, sharp low-back/hip pain, or excessive fatigue that doesn’t resolve in 24–36 hours.

- Replace one Week 12 interval session with the Week 13 HIIT structure in the next block, keeping 1–2 steady aerobic days and your strength sessions. Avoid pairing HIIT on the same day as the heaviest lower-body strength day early on.

Bottom line
- Use Weeks 4–12 to build walking intervals and strength.
- Begin low-impact HIIT at Week 13+ if all readiness boxes are ticked.
- Introduce impact-based HIIT only after passing strength/balance screens and remaining symptom-free with low-impact HIIT.

  5) Counter plank 20–25 sec (or floor plank 10–15 sec only if zero symptoms).

  - 8 goblet squats (4–7 kg)
  - 6/side reverse lunges
  - 8 incline push-ups
  - 20–30 sec suitcase carry/side

Core roadmap summary
- Weeks 4–6: Deep-core rehab only—breathing, pelvic floor, gentle TVA connection; heel slides, supine marching (tiny), bridges (short), bird dog arms-only. Avoid crunches/planks/leg lifts.
- Weeks 7–9: Anti-movement core—dead bug progressions, bird dog, Pallof holds at wall, side plank from knees, bridge march, suitcase carry drills (posture walk).
- Weeks 10–12: Stronger anti-rotation and brief plank variations—half-kneeling anti-rotation, side plank from knees with top leg straight, suitcase carries loaded, counter plank (brief), optional mini curl-ups only if zero doming/heaviness.
- Traditional abs reintroduction: Generally after 12 weeks and only if she passes readiness screens (no doming/pressure, can hold 20–25 sec low-incline plank and 30–40 sec side plank, strong dead bugs/bird dogs). Start with mini curl-ups, short planks, tiny-range bicycle taps, 2 x 6–8.

Breastfeeding-supportive nutrition
- Energy: +300–500 kcal/day above estimated maintenance while exclusively breastfeeding. Delay intentional deficit until after 6–8 weeks; if desired later, reduce by ≤250 kcal/day and monitor supply.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day (20–35 g/meal, 10–20 g/snack).
- Carbs: 45–55% of calories; include at each meal and around workouts.
- Fats: 25–35% of calories; prioritize mono/polyunsaturated fats.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; add 250–500 mL during/after harder cardio/strength; light electrolytes on hot/sweaty days.
- Micronutrients: Continue prenatal/postnatal; ensure DHA/EPA (≥200–300 mg DHA/day), choline 450–550 mg, iodine 220–290 mcg, calcium 1,000 mg, vitamin D per provider, iron as advised.
- Sample day:
  - Breakfast: Veggie omelet (2–3 eggs) + whole-grain toast with avocado; fruit.
  - Snack: Oats with milk, chia/flax, banana, peanut butter.
  - Lunch: Chicken or tofu grain bowl (quinoa/rice, roasted veg, olive oil).
  - Snack: Cottage cheese or hummus + crackers/veg; walnuts.
  - Dinner: Salmon/sardines + sweet potato + broccoli with tahini.
  - Optional pre/post: banana + yogurt pre; protein-focused meal within 1–2 hours post.
- If supply dips: add 200–300 kcal/day (carb-focused), increase fluids, rest, add an extra feeding/pump.

Scheduling example for Phase 3 (Week 12)
- Mon: Strength Circuit A + optional easy 15–20 min walk.
- Tue: Interval A cardio.
- Wed: Strength Circuit B + recovery stroll 15–20 min.
- Thu: Interval B cardio.
- Fri: Optional accessory/core or steady 30–40 min walk.
- Sat: Recovery stroll + mobility.
- Sun: Rest as needed.

Readiness to consider HIIT after Week 12
- Only if symptom-free with RPE 7 walking intervals; passes core and single-leg strength holds; ideally cleared by pelvic health PT. Introduce 1 low-impact HIIT session/week in Weeks 13–16 (e.g., 10 x 30 sec hard / 60 sec easy), monitoring closely.

Outcome targets by Week 12
- Strength: 2–3 dense circuits at RPE 7–8 using 3–8 kg household loads, lower-incline push-ups, strong suitcase carries, controlled unilateral leg work.
- Cardio: 35–40 min steady at RPE 4–5; complete peak brisk intervals without symptoms.
- Core: Symptom-free with dead bugs, bird dogs, side planks from knees, anti-rotation holds, and brief low-incline planks.

This consolidated plan keeps her safe through healing, builds meaningful strength and cardio capacity, supports breastfeeding, and peaks intensity in Phase 3 so she feels strong and confident by Week 12.

It’s home-based (mat, chair/wall/counter, backpack/water bottles). All progress is symptom-led.

Safety and guardrails
- Stop and regress if: vaginal bleeding increases, pelvic heaviness/pressure, leaking, midline doming/coning, incision/scar pain, sharp back/hip pain, dizziness, or unusual fatigue. If persistent, refer to OB/pelvic health PT.
- Exhale on exertion; no breath-holding. Ribs stacked over pelvis. Prioritize 360° breathing and pelvic floor coordination.
- Progress one variable at a time (range → tempo/pauses → reps → sets → load → stability/incline).
- Light activity only until 6-week check: walking and gentle activation, no heavy lifting or traditional abs.

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 4–6): Restore breathing, pelvic floor coordination, posture, mobility, and walking tolerance.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 7–9): Foundational strength, anti-movement core, interval walking.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 10–12): Higher intensity and density; stronger loads and unilateral work; robust cardio intervals.

Session structure template (20–35 min)
- Warm-up 5 min: 360° breathing, gentle mobility.
- Main work 15–25 min: strength or circuit as listed.
- Cool-down 3–5 min: downtraining breaths, light mobility.

WEEK-BY-WEEK PLAN

Week 4
Goals: Reconnect breath/pelvic floor, ease stiffness, short walks. RPE 3–4.
- Walking: 10–15 minutes, 5–6 days/week, flat; split if needed.
- Daily restorative (10–15 min, 5–6 days):
  1) Crocodile or side-lying 360° breathing: 6–8 breaths x 2–3.
  2) Pelvic floor awareness in hook-lying: 5–6 breath cycles x 2–3.
  3) Heel slides (tiny ROM): 6–8/side x 2.
  4) Supine marching (tiny ROM): 6/side x 2.
  5) Seated scap retraction + chin nods: 8–10 x 2.
  6) Gentle mobility: cat-cow (small), open books, calf/hip flexor 20–30 sec.
- Strength emphasis: activation only; sit-to-stand from high chair 2 x 6–8; short-range bridge 2 x 8–10; high-incline push-ups 2 x 6–8.

Week 5
Goals: Maintain walks; deepen coordination; light glute/back activation. RPE 3–4.
- Walking: 12–18 minutes, 5–6 days; optional 1–2 minutes slightly brisk if symptom-free.
- Restorative/activation (12–18 min, 5–6 days):
  1) 90/90 supported breathing: 6–8 breaths x 2–3.
  2) PF quick flicks (5 gentle 1-sec lifts) x 2–3 rounds; 3–4 slow 3–4 sec holds with full release.
  3) Supine marching (tiny ROM): 2 x 8/side.
  4) Side-lying clamshells: 2–3 x 8–10/side.
  5) Elevated counter push-ups: 2–3 x 6–8.
  6) Child’s pose lateral reaches: 20–30 sec x 2.
- Strength patterning: hip hinge to wall 2 x 8–10; bird dog arms-only 2 x 6–8/side.

Week 6
Goals: Prepare for clearance; add controlled bridges; walk longer. RPE 3–4.
- Walking: 15–20 minutes, 5–6 days, flat.
- Activation/strength (15–20 min, 5–6 days):
  1) Seated towel row (isometric squeeze): 2–3 x 8–10 with 3-sec hold.
  2) Glute bridge (short-to-moderate range): 2–3 x 8–12 with 2-sec pause.
  3) Side-lying hip abduction: 2 x 8–10/side.
  4) Sit-to-stand (high chair): 2–3 x 8–10 (3-sec down).
  5) Bird dog arms-only → add short-leg reach if symptom-free: 2 x 6–8/side.
  6) Continue breathing and PF drills.
- Checkpoint at OB visit end of week: if cleared for progressive activity and symptom-free, move to Phase 2. If not, hold Week 6 for 1–2 more weeks.

Week 7
Goals: Begin foundational strength; start anti-movement core; add intervals. RPE 5–6.
- Walking/cardio:
  - Intervals x2: 5-min warm-up → 4 x 1 min brisk (RPE 5–6) / 2 min easy → 5-min cool-down.
  - Steady x2: 20–25 min at RPE 3–4.
- Strength A (2 days):
  1) Sit-to-stand (lower chair if good control): 3 x 8–10, 3-sec down.
  2) Incline push-up (counter): 3 x 6–10.
  3) Hip hinge reach (counterbalance): 3 x 8–10.
  4) Bridge (full, 2–3 sec pause): 3 x 8–12.
  5) Bird dog (short reach): 2–3 x 5–6/side.
- Strength B (1–2 days):
  1) Supported reverse lunge: 3 x 6–8/side.
  2) Towel/isometric row: 3 x 8–10 with 3-sec squeeze.
  3) Clam → abduction combo: 2–3 x 8/side each.
  4) Dead bug arms-only → heel taps: 2–3 x 6–8/side.
- Core focus: dead bugs, bird dogs, Pallof isometric at wall 2–3 x 20–30 sec.
- Optional load: 1–2 kg goblet for squats if zero symptoms.

Week 8
Goals: Add tempo and light load; progress intervals. RPE 5–6.
- Walking/cardio:
  - Intervals x2: 5-min warm-up → 5 x 90 sec brisk (RPE 5–6) / 90 sec easy → cool-down.
  - Steady x2: 22–28 min at RPE 3–4.
- Strength A:
  1) Squat to chair, 3-sec down (optional 1–3 kg): 3 x 8–10.
  2) Incline push-up (slightly lower): 3 x 8–10.
  3) Hip hinge/RDL with 1–3 kg: 3 x 8–10.
  4) Bridge march: 3 x 6–8/side.
  5) Pallof press isometric at wall: 3 x 20–30 sec.
- Strength B:
  1) Supported reverse lunge (optional 1–2 kg): 3 x 8/side.
  2) Isometric row (step back farther): 3 x 10 with 3-sec squeezes.
  3) Side plank from knees: 3 x 15–25 sec/side.
  4) Dead bug heel taps: 3 x 8/side.

Week 9
Goals: Mild load/volume bump; intervals extended. RPE 5–6.
- Walking/cardio:
  - Intervals x2: 5-min warm-up → 6 x 2 min brisk (RPE 5–6) / 90 sec easy → cool-down.
  - Steady x2: 25–30 min at RPE 3–4; 1 optional recovery stroll 15–20 min.
- Strength A:
  1) Split squat (supported; optional 1–3 kg): 3 x 6–8/side.
  2) Incline push-up: 3 x 8–12 (lower if 12 easy).
  3) RDL 1–3 kg: 3 x 10–12.
  4) Bridge with 5-sec top hold: 3 x 8–10.
  5) Bird dog longer reach: 3 x 6–8/side.
- Strength B:
  1) Step-ups (8–12 in; optional load): 3 x 8/side.
  2) Wall anti-rotation press (farther step-out): 3 x 8–10 with 3-sec hold.
  3) Side plank from knees 20–30 sec or posture suitcase carry (no/1 kg): 3 x 20–30 sec/side.
  4) Dead bug alternating arms/legs: 3 x 6–8/side.

Week 10
Goals: Phase 3 begins—intensity and density up; stronger core; cardio harder. RPE 6–7.
- Cardio:
  - Interval A: 3 x 4 min strong brisk (RPE 6–7) / 2 min easy, with warm-up/cool-down (27–30 min).
  - Interval B: 10 x 45 sec fast walk (RPE ~7) / 60 sec easy, with warm-up/cool-down (27–30 min).
  - Steady x2: 28–35 min at RPE 3–4.
  - Recovery day: 15–20 min easy + mobility.
- Strength Circuit A (2–3 rounds; 20–30 sec between moves; 60–90 sec between rounds; RPE 6–7):
  1) Goblet squat 3–6 kg: 10 reps, 3-sec eccentric, 1-sec pause.
  2) RDL 3–6 kg: 10–12 reps, 2-sec pause mid-shin.
  3) Step-up (10–12 in) hold 2–4 kg: 8/side, slow lower.
  4) Incline push-up (counter/table): 10–12.
  5) Bridge march: 8/side with 2-sec pause.
  6) Half-kneeling anti-rotation press at wall: 25–30 sec/side.
- Strength Circuit B (2 rounds; RPE 6–7):
  1) Split squat 2–4 kg: 8/side, 3-sec lower.
  2) Backpack row (light–moderate): 10–12 with 1–2-sec squeeze.
  3) Single-leg RDL reach (BW): 8/side.
  4) Side plank from knees with top leg straight: 20–25 sec/side.
  5) Suitcase carry 2–3 kg: 25–30 sec/side.
- Optional conditioning/core finisher (1 day; EMOM 12 min):
  - Min 1: Marching step-ups 45 sec.
  - Min 2: Incline plank shoulder taps (high counter) 10–12/side, then box breathing.

Week 11
Goals: Heavier-for-her loads; more unilateral; lower push-up angle; cardio variety. RPE 7–8.
- Cardio:
  - Interval A pyramid: 2 / 3 / 4 / 3 / 2 min brisk (RPE 6–7) with equal easy between; add warm-up/cool-down (32–35 min).
  - Interval B: 6 x 90 sec up-tempo (RPE 6–7) / 90 sec easy; with warm-up/cool-down (25–28 min).
  - Steady x2: one at 30–35 min RPE 4–5; one at 25–30 min RPE 3–4.
  - Recovery stroll: 15–20 min easy.
- Circuit A (3 rounds; 20–30 sec between moves; RPE 7–8):
  1) Goblet split squat 3–6 kg: 8/side, 3-sec eccentric.
  2) RDL 4–7 kg: 10–12.
  3) Incline push-up (low angle, sturdy table): 10–12.
  4) Step-downs (slow 3-sec lower): 8/side.
  5) Suitcase carry 3–5 kg: 30 sec/side.
- Circuit B (2–3 rounds; RPE 7):
  1) Goblet squat 4–7 kg: 10–12.
  2) Single-leg RDL reach (add 1–2 kg if balanced): 8/side.
  3) Backpack row (moderate): 10–12 with 2-sec squeeze.
  4) Side plank from knees: 25–30 sec/side.
  5) Dead bug alternating with long exhale: 8/side.

Week 12
Goals: Peak week—dense circuits; confident loads; strong cardio. RPE 7–8.
- Cardio:
  - Interval A peak repeats: 6 x 3 min strong brisk (RPE 7) / 90 sec easy, with warm-up/cool-down (35–38 min).
  - Interval B density: 12 x 60 sec fast walk (RPE 7) / 60 sec easy, with warm-up/cool-down (34–36 min).
  - Steady x1–2: 30–40 min at RPE 4–5 (split if needed).
  - Recovery day: 15–20 min easy + mobility.
- Strength Circuit A (3 rounds; minimal rest between moves; RPE 7–8):
  1) Goblet squat 5–8 kg: 10–12 (3-sec down, brief pause).
  2) RDL 5–8 kg: 12.
  3) Split squat 3–5 kg: 8–10/side.
  4) Incline push-up (lowest safe angle): 10–12.
  5) Single-leg bridge: 8/side, controlled.
  6) Anti-rotation press or suitcase carry 4–6 kg: 35–40 sec/side.
- Strength Circuit B (2–3 rounds; density focus; RPE 7–8):
  1) Step-up (hold 2–4 kg at chest): 10/side.
  2) Backpack row (moderate–heavy for her): 12 reps + 2–3-sec hold last rep.
  3) Single-leg RDL reach (1–3 kg): 8–10/side.
  4) Side plank progression (knees with top leg straight or staggered): 20–30 sec/side.
  5) Counter plank 20–25 sec (or floor plank 10–15 sec only if zero symptoms).
- Optional finisher (RPE 7–8; only if symptom-free; 8-minute AMRAP):
  - 8 goblet squats (4–7 kg)
  - 6/side reverse lunges
  - 8 incline push-ups
  - 20–30 sec suitcase carry/side

Core roadmap summary
- Weeks 4–6: Deep-core rehab only—breathing, pelvic floor, gentle TVA connection; heel slides, supine marching (tiny), bridges (short), bird dog arms-only. Avoid crunches/planks/leg lifts.
- Weeks 7–9: Anti-movement core—dead bug progressions, bird dog, Pallof holds at wall, side plank from knees, bridge march, suitcase carry drills (posture walk).
- Weeks 10–12: Stronger anti-rotation and brief plank variations—half-kneeling anti-rotation, side plank from knees with top leg straight, suitcase carries loaded, counter plank (brief), optional mini curl-ups only if zero doming/heaviness.
- Traditional abs reintroduction: Generally after 12 weeks and only if she passes readiness screens (no doming/pressure, can hold 20–25 sec low-incline plank and 30–40 sec side plank, strong dead bugs/bird dogs). Start with mini curl-ups, short planks, tiny-range bicycle taps, 2 x 6–8.

Breastfeeding-supportive nutrition
- Energy: +300–500 kcal/day above estimated maintenance while exclusively breastfeeding. Delay intentional deficit until after 6–8 weeks; if desired later, reduce by ≤250 kcal/day and monitor supply.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day (20–35 g/meal, 10–20 g/snack).
- Carbs: 45–55% of calories; include at each meal and around workouts.
- Fats: 25–35% of calories; prioritize mono/polyunsaturated fats.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; add 250–500 mL during/after harder cardio/strength; light electrolytes on hot/sweaty days.
- Micronutrients: Continue prenatal/postnatal; ensure DHA/EPA (≥200–300 mg DHA/day), choline 450–550 mg, iodine 220–290 mcg, calcium 1,000 mg, vitamin D per provider, iron as advised.
- Sample day:
  - Breakfast: Veggie omelet (2–3 eggs) + whole-grain toast with avocado; fruit.
  - Snack: Oats with milk, chia/flax, banana, peanut butter.
  - Lunch: Chicken or tofu grain bowl (quinoa/rice, roasted veg, olive oil).
  - Snack: Cottage cheese or hummus + crackers/veg; walnuts.
  - Dinner: Salmon/sardines + sweet potato + broccoli with tahini.
  - Optional pre/post: banana + yogurt pre; protein-focused meal within 1–2 hours post.
- If supply dips: add 200–300 kcal/day (carb-focused), increase fluids, rest, add an extra feeding/pump.

Scheduling example for Phase 3 (Week 12)
- Mon: Strength Circuit A + optional easy 15–20 min walk.
- Tue: Interval A cardio.
- Wed: Strength Circuit B + recovery stroll 15–20 min.
- Thu: Interval B cardio.
- Fri: Optional accessory/core or steady 30–40 min walk.
- Sat: Recovery stroll + mobility.
- Sun: Rest as needed.

Readiness to consider HIIT after Week 12
- Only if symptom-free with RPE 7 walking intervals; passes core and single-leg strength holds; ideally cleared by pelvic health PT. Introduce 1 low-impact HIIT session/week in Weeks 13–16 (e.g., 10 x 30 sec hard / 60 sec easy), monitoring closely.

Outcome targets by Week 12
- Strength: 2–3 dense circuits at RPE 7–8 using 3–8 kg household loads, lower-incline push-ups, strong suitcase carries, controlled unilateral leg work.
- Cardio: 35–40 min steady at RPE 4–5; complete peak brisk intervals without symptoms.
- Core: Symptom-free with dead bugs, bird dogs, side planks from knees, anti-rotation holds, and brief low-incline planks.

This consolidated plan keeps her safe through healing, builds meaningful strength and cardio capacity, supports breastfeeding, and peaks intensity in Phase 3 so she feels strong and confident by Week 12.
